close_reason: Atom-keyed maps now use the language's node-global name order on every construction, mutation, and lookup path.
description:
## Two answers to one question

"How do two atoms order?" has two implementations that disagree.

```
fn main() do
  dbg(Kernel.compare(:z, :a))              #=> 1        :z after :a
  dbg(Enum.sort([:z, :a, :m]))             #=> [:a, :m, :z]
  dbg(Map.keys(%{z: 1, a: 2, m: 3}))       #=> [:z, :a, :m]
  dbg(Map.keys(%{"z" => 1, "a" => 2, "m" => 3}))   #=> ["a", "m", "z"]
end
```

Identical on `interp` and `run`, so this is not a door disagreement -- both doors agree on the wrong thing. Binary keys sort by content, as documented. Atom keys do not sort by name.

Rewriting the literal in any order gives the same answer, so it is not insertion order either: `%{a: 2, m: 3, z: 1}` and `%{m: 3, z: 1, a: 2}` both come out `[:z, :a, :m]`. And it is not alphabetical-by-coincidence -- `%{qzx: 1, abc: 2, mno: 3}` comes out `[:qzx, :abc, :mno]`.

It is intern id: the order the atoms were first seen across the whole compiled program.

## Where

- `cmp_any_value` / `fz_value_cmp_ref` (`runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs`) orders atoms through `cmp_atom_names(process, a, b)`, by NAME. It takes the process precisely because the name table lives on the node -- `.agent/docs/semantic-authorities.md` calls this out: "atoms order by NAME, because ... ordering by id would depend on which atom the program mentioned first."
- `map_key_cmp_any` (`runtime/src/heap/key_cmp.rs:35`) takes NO process. It cannot reach the name table, so after the category and bitstring cases it falls through to `a.raw().cmp(&b.raw())` -- and an atom's raw payload is its intern id.

The missing process parameter is the whole bug, visible in the signature.

## Why it matters

`Map.keys/1`, `Map.values/1` and `Map.to_list/1` on an atom-keyed map answer in an order that depends on which atoms the rest of the program happened to mention first. Adding an unrelated `:a` somewhere earlier can reorder an unrelated map's iteration. That is the exact hazard the term order was made process-aware to avoid.

Lookup is unaffected: a flat sorted array only needs the array's order to agree with its key equality, and id order does agree with itself. This is an ordering-visibility bug, not a corruption bug.

## Two comments this makes false

`lib/map.fz`'s header says iteration order "is by key. For binary keys that matches Elixir exactly. For atom keys it cannot: Elixir orders atoms by an internal identity fz does not share, so `Map.keys(%{a: 1, b: 2, c: 3})` is `[:c, :a, :b]` there and `[:a, :b, :c]` here." fz shares exactly that kind of internal identity; `[:a, :b, :c]` is a coincidence of those three atoms' intern order, not name ordering.

`.agent/docs/semantic-authorities.md`'s "Map key identity and order" entry states the agreement between order and equality, which holds, but does not record that map atom order and the term order are different orders.

## Fix

Give the map comparator the process and route atoms through `cmp_atom_names`, so a map's key order is the term order. Then the comment becomes true as written and `Map.keys/1` agrees with `Enum.sort/1`.

The cost to weigh: `map_key_cmp_any` is on the map write path (`alloc_map_slots`, `alloc_map_refs_bits` both sort and dedup through it), so this makes atom-keyed map construction do a name comparison per step instead of an integer compare. Measure before and after against the map allocation goldens.

title: [BUG] Atoms order by name in the term order and by intern id in a map, so map iteration order is program-dependent
